Paloma Rivera: Hey all — hitting a weird one with the Python SDK streaming iterator. I cancel the async generator on client shutdown, but occasionally the same iterator appears to resume and emits more chunks after the cancel. Repro is flaky.

Kai Chen: ugh. Do you have a short repro? sounds like an asyncio task getting re-scheduled or a socket reconnect.

Paloma Rivera: Minimal repro: async for chunk in client.stream(...):
    yield chunk

then on SIGINT we call `task.cancel()` and `await client.close()` — most of the time it stops, but sometimes extra chunks trickle in.

Mike L.: can you paste the stream call? is this using SSE over httpx or raw chunked response?

Paloma Rivera: httpx + our streaming wrapper. Code looks like:```py
async def stream(prompt):
    async with client.stream("/v1/streams", json={"prompt": prompt}) as resp:
        async for line in resp.aiter_lines():
            yield parse(line)
```
Cancel flow: we cancel the consumer task, then call `await resp.aclose()` in the wrapper finalizer.

sara: I wonder if `resp.aiter_lines()` yields a partial buffer after a close race. httpx has some weirdness where background tasks flush. Have you tried `resp.aread()` handling or wrapping the iterator with an explicit `try: finally: await resp.aclose()`?

Paloma Rivera: I added `finally: await resp.aclose()` but still saw a couple of cases where chunks came through ~2s after cancel. Could be keepalive/reconnect on connection pool?

Kai Chen: Is the SDK exposing a public async iterator (PEP 525)? We had a couple bugs where `__anext__` could be re-entered after a cancellation due to awaiting an async generator finalizer. Maybe the generator finalizer isn't protected with a guard flag, so it can resume when the event loop processes pending callbacks.

Mike L.: That rings a bell. I think we had an internal issue where the generator's `aclose()` was not awaited before task cancel completed, so GC/weakref finalizer kicked in later and reopened the socket.

Paloma Rivera: I can try forcing `await gen.aclose()` in the cancel path. Quick test: wrap the iterator like `agen = client.stream(...); task = loop.create_task(_consume(agen));` on cancel: `await agen.aclose(); task.cancel()` — will run this today.

dev-bot: New issue created: #2785 — "py-sdk: async stream resumes after cancel / generator finalizer race" (assigned to kai).

Kai Chen: Thanks bot. Paloma, if you can add a minimal CI test that cancels during iteration and asserts socket is closed (or no more chunks) that would be huge. I can follow up with a patch adding an `_closed` guard in generator finalizer and ensuring `aclose()` is idempotent.

Paloma Rivera: Will do. One weird edge: I saw duplicate final chunks when canceling while the server was sending the final chunk — looks like both the server close and our finalizer both emit the terminal chunk. Will try to reproduce deterministically.

Mike L.: sounds like we need to dedupe terminal events at the SDK layer. Maybe the stream wrapper should track `seen_terminal` and swallow duplicates. Also update typings to indicate `aclose()` is required for graceful shutdown.

sara: small DX ask: can we add a note in the quickstart about shutdown/cancel best practices for async streams? People assume canceling the task is enough but with pooled httpx backends you may need `await client.close()` or explicit `agen.aclose()`.

Kai Chen: Agreed. I'll land a fix and a docs blurb. Paloma — if you can attach your flaky log snippet (timestamps + request ids) to the issue that helps.

Paloma Rivera: attaching logs to #2785 now. thanks y'all. Will report back after the forced `aclose()` test. :pray:

Mike L.: follow-up: added a quick prototype PR to gate finalizer emission (won't land yet) — saves duplicate terminal events and marks streams closed synchronously in the wrapper. Leaving comments on #2785.

Paloma Rivera: repro confirms `await agen.aclose()` prevents the resume in local tests. flaky cloud repro still possible but much rarer. Good enough to block on fix + tests.

Kai Chen: cool. moving to in-progress. will update when PR is ready.

sara: created a short onboarding note in the docs repo with explicit shutdown snippet and a note about `aclose()`. filing a docs PR to link from quickstart.

Paloma Rivera: thanks!"
